messages.subject: Re: Calling a R shiny app from other applications via encoded url and get it to return a value to them
messages.subject_clean: Calling a R shiny app from other applications via encoded url and get it to return a value to them
messages.body_plain:
Hi RN, I don't know what is the level of risk you're willing to have in this project. Joe has been working on a native Shiny API, but it is under development and it's likely it will still change a lot before we release into the master branch. So, if you need something stable, it may be a while (I can't say exactly how long, but at very least, a few weeks). However, if you just need something quick right now, you can use the implementation that we have today (this is kept in an undocumented branch on Github).

First, you need to install that branch of Shiny:
devtools::install_github("rstudio/shiny@feature/api")

Second, for ease of explanation here, let's also set a particular port to listen for your Shiny app (and make it not pop up every time):
options(shiny.launch.browser = FALSE, shiny.port = 7791)

Then. let's say your app looks like this:
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  selectInput(inputId = "n_breaks",
    label = "Number of bins in histogram (approximate):",
    choices = c(10, 20, 35, 50),
    selected = 20),

  checkboxInput(inputId = "individual_obs",
    label = strong("Show individual observations"),
    value = FALSE),

  plotOutput(outputId = "main_plot", height = "300px")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$main_plot <- renderPlot({
    hist(faithful$eruptions,
      probability = TRUE,
      breaks = as.numeric(input$n_breaks),
      xlab = "Duration (minutes)",
      main = "Geyser eruption duration")

    if (input$individual_obs) {
      rug(faithful$eruptions)
    }
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

So, you have two inputs (`n_breaks` and `individual_obs`) and one plot output (`main_plot`). It's pretty basic, it looks like this:

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-DrlrX_0MlJU/WJF2MOf7qDI/AAAAAAAAAH0/jbHt7-RlryQzWPwiiletkXQZHmFl85yVgCLcB/s1600/Screen%2BShot%2B2017-02-01%2Bat%2B5.45.01%2BAM.png>

So, let's say you want to make this plot available though a URL, where you can also specify the two inputs that control it (`n_breaks` and `individual_obs`). Simply add this to your server function (notice that the content of the function is exactly the same, it's only the name of the object and the function itself that have changed...):

  session$api$main_plot <- servePlot({
    hist(faithful$eruptions,
      probability = TRUE,
      breaks = as.numeric(input$n_breaks),
      xlab = "Duration (minutes)",
      main = "Geyser eruption duration")

    if (input$individual_obs) {
      rug(faithful$eruptions)
    }
  })

Now, if you visit the same URL, you get the same app, no problem. But now, you can also visit another URL (this one, static) with the name of the object and the arguments passed in as parameters: http://127.0.0.1:7791/api/main_plot?n_breaks=25&individual_obs="T" <http://127.0.0.1:7791/api/main_plot?n_breaks=25&individual_obs=%22T%22>:

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-xcV6FuOewCI/WJF3Wis3pnI/AAAAAAAAAIA/FupAX5seyEcYi2PUAO8UKHzJynozXiNZACLcB/s1600/Screen%2BShot%2B2017-02-01%2Bat%2B5.45.23%2BAM.png>

These two URLs are not really related in any way. In fact, each time that you click "enter" on the API URL, Shiny will start up your app, run it once with the params you give it and immediately shut it down, saving only the artifact that you served with the serve function.

Try changing the values of the inputs on the URL and you'll get a different plot. E.g.:  http://127.0.0.1:7791/api/main_plot?n_breaks=50&individual_obs="F" <http://127.0.0.1:7791/api/main_plot?n_breaks=40&individual_obs=%22F%22>:

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-rgpEGbWb7oo/WJF4MtMSmZI/AAAAAAAAAII/UNmhXyLhA683z6IZ6mne14orME7LIOZFACLcB/s1600/Screen%2BShot%2B2017-02-01%2Bat%2B5.54.40%2BAM.png>

Hope this helps you somewhat! Just keep in mind that this is still a very experimental feature that may change quite a bit in the immediate future... If this is enough for you, you can always just make sure you're on the same version of Shiny (same commit SHA), but that's obviously not a scalable answer if your app changes...

messages.body_plain:
Spoke too soon. I managed to make my code into modules but I cannot find the right way to insert them dynamically.

I global.R I have a variable module_names that has the names of the modules.
In server.R I then have:

lapply(seq_along(module_names),
       function(i){ callModule(get(module_names[i]), paste0("name",i))
                  }
           )

That works. As before my problem is the ui.R. Right now my attempt is this:

lapply(seq_along(module_names),
       function(i){ do.call(paste0(module_names[i],"UI"),list(id = paste0("name",i)))
                  }
       )

The app loads and there are no errors but I have "tab-7636-1 tab-pane active" displayed instead of the tab I am inserting.

Any hint would be highly appreciated. Also if there is a bit more elegant way to do this.

messages.subject_clean: Shiny and Bookdown
messages.body_plain:
Hi
It might be obvious, but I haven't found how to include a shiny app in a bookdown document.
There is an example for including the miniUI in the documentation, but not on how to include an own app.
I tried to include "myapp" in the subdirectory "myapp" either as an integrated file (app.R) or as the two files server.R and ui.R using include_app("myapp") or runApp("myapp"), but this doesn't work.
Thanks
Renger

messages.subject: Re: Shiny and Bookdown
messages.subject_clean: Shiny and Bookdown
messages.body_plain:
You cannot embed a local Shiny app in a bookdown document. You can
only embed a published Shiny app through its URL.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: Bootstrap Tour in Shiny apps?
messages.subject_clean: Bootstrap Tour in Shiny apps?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Andras,

Thanks so much for the link. This is exactly what I was looking for and also looks much preferable to using Bootstrap tours as well. I've been playing around with it, but so far am experiencing some weird issues. Using infoBox() in ui.R works great. But in my case I need to do it all in server.R by passing the steps option in the intorjs() options list, like in the second example on the repo page. This allows me to use the position option in the reactive data frame, steps(), for each step as well as more dynamic content. It also keeps ui.R much cleaner if it is a big app that would be littered with many introBox() calls.

I haven't posted an issue on github yet because I haven't reproduced a simple example. But what I am seeing happening is a couple dynamically generated steps display fine and many more tour steps display in the far top left corner of the screen, or sometimes in the top left of some other panel- but nowhere near the input or output whose ID is referenced. When I inspect the page in my browser, it looks like using infoBox() in ui.R properly inserts the correct div around the browser element so that introjs() can display the step near the element. But the same step if passed to the steps option list in server.R, will not insert a div at all, leading to the intro text box showing up somewhere else, usually the corner of the screen.

If I can come up with a small reproducible example, I'll share here and post a github issue, but for now I'm not sure what is really happening. I would love to pass a nice, clean set of vectors of element and intro in server.R and not insert a ton of infoBox() calls in ui.R, but it seems like at least for now that may be the only option. I haven't found any references online to people having a similar issue so I could be using introjs() incorrectly somehow.

Regards,
Matt

On Thursday, January 26, 2017 at 12:48:00 AM UTC-7, Andrew Sali wrote:
> Hi Matt,
>
> You might be interested in taking a look at the 'rintrojs' package. It can be used for app tours and it works well with Shiny.
>
> https://github.com/carlganz/rintrojs <https://www.google.com/url?q=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fcarlganz%2Frintrojs&sa=D&sntz=1&usg=AFQjCNHFY3nzZrEOv_17ZnU3BWNX3VG6og>
>
> Best,
>
> Andras
>
> On Wednesday, January 25, 2017 at 3:46:37 PM UTC+1, Matthew Leonawicz wrote:
> >
> > Hi,
> >
> > I am wondering if there is a recommended way for integrating a Bootstrap Tour (http://bootstraptour.com/) into a shiny app? While I've seen non-shiny web applications that make use of tours - where tour steps describe the app, the source data, how to use it, and show examples of plots and maps in the tour step modals, etc - I haven't seen any examples of this with Shiny. So I am thinking this would all have to be written in html/css/js and sourced into the app. Or is there some bootstrap tour functionality for R Shiny or related packages somewhere already?
> >
> > This would be great for apps that might appear overwhelmingly complex to a user not intimately familiar with the breadth or depth of data, input options, and complicated analyses made available by the app. Because Shiny apps lend themselves by design to such complex content dissemination, Shiny seems like a perfect use case for app tours, but I am not sure exactly what that would look like in terms of wrapper function implementation to make it a convenient widget for a wide R user audience.
> >
> > Matt

On Wednesday, February 1, 2017 at 8:49:33 AM UTC-7, Matthew Leonawicz wrote:
> Hi Andras,
>
> Thanks so much for the link. This is exactly what I was looking for and also looks much preferable to using Bootstrap tours as well. I've been playing around with it, but so far am experiencing some weird issues. Using infoBox() in ui.R works great. But in my case I need to do it all in server.R by passing the steps option in the intorjs() options list, like in the second example on the repo page. This allows me to use the position option in the reactive data frame, steps(), for each step as well as more dynamic content. It also keeps ui.R much cleaner if it is a big app that would be littered with many introBox() calls.
>
> I haven't posted an issue on github yet because I haven't reproduced a simple example. But what I am seeing happening is a couple dynamically generated steps display fine and many more tour steps display in the far top left corner of the screen, or sometimes in the top left of some other panel- but nowhere near the input or output whose ID is referenced. When I inspect the page in my browser, it looks like using infoBox() in ui.R properly inserts the correct div around the browser element so that introjs() can display the step near the element. But the same step if passed to the steps option list in server.R, will not insert a div at all, leading to the intro text box showing up somewhere else, usually the corner of the screen.
>
> If I can come up with a small reproducible example, I'll share here and post a github issue, but for now I'm not sure what is really happening. I would love to pass a nice, clean set of vectors of element and intro in server.R and not insert a ton of infoBox() calls in ui.R, but it seems like at least for now that may be the only option. I haven't found any references online to people having a similar issue so I could be using introjs() incorrectly somehow.

messages.subject: Re: How can I change the background color by pressing an action button? (shinydashboard)
messages.subject_clean: How can I change the background color by pressing an action button? (shinydashboard)
messages.body_plain:
Here's one way to do (assuming you only want this action to be taken up one time):

## app.R ##
library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)

ui <- dashboardPage(
  dashboardHeader(),
  dashboardSidebar( actionButton("go", "Change color") ),
  dashboardBody()
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  observeEvent(input$go, {
    insertUI("head", "beforeEnd",
      tags$style(HTML('.content-wrapper, .left-side { background-color: #123456; }'))
    )
  }, ignoreInit = TRUE, once = TRUE)
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

messages.body_plain:

It could easily be https causing the difference if you have a proxy or two between your browser and server. Proxies tend to muck around with http requests (trying to be "helpful") much more than https.

messages.subject: Reactive Input
messages.subject_clean: Reactive Input
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I've created a shiny app  <https://nzgwynn.shinyapps.io/shiny/>but would love some suggestions or examples that do something similar to what I'm doing. On the General Input tab, the numericInput - No. of matching variables  - needs to use to develop the UI in the second tab. I'm trying to do something like this, but I'm not sure of the format:

tabPanel("Matching Variables Info",

             tabPanel("Matching Variables Info",

             reactive(
               switch(
                 input$NoVars,

                 NoV = input$NoVars
                 C = sapply(1:NoV, function(i){paste0("cols",i)})
                 L = sapply(1:NoV, function(i){paste0("label",i)})
                 W = sapply(1:NoV, function(i){paste0("weight",i)})
                 S = sapply(1:NoV, function(i){paste0("slider",i)})

                 for(i seq_along(1:NoVars)){
                   selectInput(C[i], "Variable to randomize:",
                               col.labs),
                   textInput(L[i], label = h3("Label for variable:"),
                             value = "Label for variable Here"),
                   sliderInput(W[i],
                               "Weight for variable:",
                               min = 1,  max = 5, value = 1),
                   sliderInput(S[i], "Min and max for variable",
                               min = 0, max = 2, value = c(0, 1))
                 } # for loop
               ) #switch
             )#reactive

 On the second tab "Variables to be randomized:" is not as I'd like it to be. I used this:

lhs = colnames(D)
l.cols = length(lhs)
rhs = sapply(1:l.cols, function(i){paste0("col",i)})
col.labs = sapply(1:l.cols, function(i){paste0(lhs[i], '" = "', rhs[i])})

where D is a dataframe with column names. For some reason the UI is picking up the rhs despite the quote which I thought told it not to. I'd like to be able to upload any dataframe and have the coding work so that's why I've done it that way. Any suggestions would be great.

Thanks,
gwynn

The github issue has been updated and is being worked on. If you are having issues with incorrect location for tooltip and element highlighting placements in the browser such as the upper left corner of your screen using the rintrojs package, or if you want to help, see here:

https://github.com/carlganz/rintrojs/issues/16

There is also an overlapping issue with using rintrojs on reactive inputs wrapped in conditionalPanel. See the same github issue above.

Anyhow, this seems superior to Bootstrap tours. I second the recommendation for using intro JS via the rintrojs package.

Matt

messages.subject: Re: scoping and input forms
messages.subject_clean: scoping and input forms
messages.body_plain:
I'm not sure this is the best solution, but I may not have understood the flexibility in the <<- operator used in the cited examples to update the data entered via the input form. For example, in Dean Atali's example, <<- assigns the dataset "responses" to the highest level space (shared across users). However, this is not mandatory, since it appears to search upward until it finds the named object. So simply by assigning "responses" = NULL within  shinyServer(function(input, output)), the dataset "responses" will only be shared within the browser session. which was the goal.

There is probably a better solution using "modules", but this seems to work and requires only that the dataset first be defined in the desired environment.

Curiously, the article on scoping  https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/scoping.html   seems to suggest that anything defined within shinyServer(function( should appear in .GlobalEnv, which is seen only by the individual browser session. But if I explicitly assign("responses", responses, .GlobalEnv), it is not restricted to the browser session.

Atul

On Saturday, February 4, 2017 at 8:55:47 PM UTC-6, Atul Sharma wrote:
> I've been reading posts about using input forms to mimic Google forms e.g. a nice example from Dean Atali at
>
> http://deanattali.com/2015/06/14/mimicking-google-form-shiny/#build-inputs
>
> or a full CRUD interface http://ipub.com/shiny-crud-app/
>
> But I don't understand how to keep the resulting input data from other users of a Shiny app. In the examples, the input data handling functions are in the header (shared environment), which makes the data available to all users. If I move them to within the shinyServer(function(input, output)), they no longer share data between the update/ save etc functions. I had expected that this location would make them available to the individual browser session; at least that's my take on the scoping rules at
>
>  https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/scoping.html
>
> But this doesn't appear to be the case. Any suggestions as to how I might sandbox the data to avoid leakage across users.
>
> Thanks
>
> Atul
>

messages.subject: Making data available across all apps for every user.
messages.subject_clean: Making data available across all apps for every user.
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
I working on a project where we want to deliver our internal BI reports using R and shinydashboard. We have installed shinyserver on a virtual ubuntu server and everything is working fine.

I have several apps each covering a different view of the data and as each app is its own dashboard, each app contains several ouputs (charts, tables, etc.). We display the apps in an iframe on an asp page. The menu on the asp page basically points to a new app to display.

Each app/webpage, reads the same large raw dataset from a csv which is updated nightly. Depending on the app and what is being displayed, different data manipulations are required.

There are many of my colleagues who view the apps each day and each time a colleague views the app it reads the csv anew.  So for every app and for every colleague the dataset is repeatedly read.

Is it possible to read the dataset once and then make it available for all apps and all users until it is refreshed so that all that is required is the data manipulations for each each chart or table the app displays?

Thank Andrew.

  # Application title
  withMathJax(),
  uiOutput('mj1'),

  # Sidebar panel

    #Selector for file upload

  })

  #observe the genes list and update genes drop down
  observe({
    values$df_data = filedata()
    genesList = values$df_data[1]
    updateSelectInput(session, "gene", "Genes ", unique(genesList))
  })

  #observe changes in the genes dropdown and update allele drop down
  observeEvent(input$gene, {
      cvsInput = filedata()
      cvsInput.gene.sub <- as.data.frame(subset(cvsInput, Gene == input$gene, drop=FALSE, byrow=TRUE))
      updateSelectInput(session, "allele", "Allele ", cvsInput.gene.sub[, 6])
  })

  #observe allele drop down and populate population drop down
  observeEvent(input$allele, {
      cvsInput = filedata()
      cvsInput.allele.sub <- as.data.frame(subset(cvsInput, Allele == input$allele & Gene == input$gene, drop=FALSE, byrow=TRUE))
      updateSelectInput(session, "population", "Population ", cvsInput.allele.sub[, 12])
  })

  #observe population drop down and show selected rows in text output
  observeEvent(input$goButton, {
    input$goButton
    isolate({
     cvsInput = filedata()
       #perform formula calc

        output$plot1 <- renderPlot({
          plot(plotValue)
        })# end render plot

    }) # end isolate

  })# end observeEvent(input$goButton)

})# end shiny server

Any help would be greatly appreciated, thanks!

messages.body_plain:
I broke the server function down, to untangle it as follows:

1- I made ABC_Input reactive, so that you can track the changes and re-use it.
2- I got observeEvent out of renderTable
3- I made Data_new reactive and outside of renderTable (in case you will re-use it or sth). Inside it, I called ABC_Input()to get the reactive value and then make calculations.
4- I added renderTable at the end, calling Data_new()

In each step, I made sure the required values are available using req(), I might be missing sth, but you can start from here and make your checks.

server <- function (input, output,session){

  ## reactive value to read the csv file in ----------
  ABC_Input <- reactive({
    req(input$file1)
    data.frame(read.csv(input$file1$datapath))
  })

  ## observe input$file1 to update the input$rev_col ------------
  observeEvent(input$file1,{
    updateSelectInput(session,
                      inputId = "rev_col",
                      choices = names(ABC_Input()))
  }
  )

  ## Data_new as reactive (could be used in other chuncks)---------------
  Data_new <- reactive({
    req(input$rev_col)
    # now ABC_Input is reactive, so you need to call ABC_Input()
    Data_new <- ABC_Input()[order(ABC_Input()[input$rev_col], decreasing = T),]
    # Create cumsum variable
    Data_new$Rev_CumSum = cumsum(Data_new[input$rev_col])
    #Create Percentages of CumSum
    Data_new$Percent_Rev_Cum <- Data_new$Rev_CumSum / sum(Data_new[input$rev_col])

    return(Data_new)
  })

  ## render table of Data_new() -------------------
  output$str <- renderTable({
    req(input$rev_col)
    Data_new()
  })

}

You are welcome. I suggest you take a step back and try the following:

Make sure you understand the difference between the reactive expression, which give the recipe of getting a certain value, depending on inputs or other reactive values
x <- reactive({....})
and getting it's value at a certain moment using:
x()

Try to write element by element and print the output or try to inspect it to see what you get at each point
Break things down
If you need to recalculate the same value in different chunks, write the reactive expression once, and reuse it
If a block performs many tasks(calculate values, save, render...etc.) , try to break it to multiple blocks
Then it will take less time for you and others to isolate the problem/s.

messages.subject: Re: Making data available across all apps for every user.
messages.subject_clean: Making data available across all apps for every user.
messages.body_plain:
It is not possible to load once for all apps, since each app runs in its own process (or possibly more than one process per app if you're using Shiny Server Pro). However, it is possible to load once for all users within a single process by either using global.R as Bob said or just by inserting the variable above/outside the shiny server function. https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/scoping.html

Other tips:

- use the readr package instead of read.csv, it's much, much faster
- consider saving the CSV data as .rds or feather formats, this may or may not be faster
- if you need the data to stay up to date automatically (i.e. apps update live when file on disk changes), take a look at reactiveFileReader

  ns <- shiny::NS(id)
  shiny::selectInput(ns("dynamic_select"), label,
                     choices = NULL, multiple = multiple, width = "100%")

dynamicSelect <- function(input, output, session, the_data, column, default_select = NULL){

  observe({
    shiny::validate(
      shiny::need(the_data(),"Fetching data")
    )
    dt <- the_data()

    testthat::expect_is(dt, "data.frame")
    testthat::expect_is(column, "character")

                      choices = choice,

  })

  return(reactive(input$dynamic_select))

}

messages.subject: Re: Does using same reactive expression multiple times have performance penalty?
messages.subject_clean: Does using same reactive expression multiple times have performance penalty?
messages.body_plain:
Reactive expressions are cached, and they are only re-calculated when their dependencies change. Calling the same reactive expression many times should have no effect on performance (assuming the dependencies don't change).

The only way this may be a problem is if you have an observer for a button, for example, that, when clicked, causes the dependencies for the reactive expression to change, which is then re-computed (if its value is important for any currently non-hidden output on your app). However, in an opposite example, an observer for a button that, when clicked, only invokes, the reactive expression, should be exactly the same (in terms of performance) as not having that observer at all in the app.

Because they are inside the parameters of renderPlot, renderDataTable, I didn't find a method to assign the expression to variable first then use the variable later.
>
> I'm wondering if this usage will have a performance penalty. I felt it shouldn't but my app is becoming slower when I have more features and reactive expression usage added.
>
> Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: Does using same reactive expression multiple times have performance penalty?
messages.subject_clean: Does using same reactive expression multiple times have performance penalty?
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for confirmation. I'll check other places to look for the performance problem then.

On Wednesday, February 8, 2017 at 6:35:30 AM UTC-5, Bárbara Borges wrote:
> Reactive expressions are cached, and they are only re-calculated when their dependencies change. Calling the same reactive expression many times should have no effect on performance (assuming the dependencies don't change).
>
> The only way this may be a problem is if you have an observer for a button, for example, that, when clicked, causes the dependencies for the reactive expression to change, which is then re-computed (if its value is important for any currently non-hidden output on your app). However, in an opposite example, an observer for a button that, when clicked, only invokes, the reactive expression, should be exactly the same (in terms of performance) as not having that observer at all in the app.
>
> On Tuesday, February 7, 2017 at 6:34:28 PM UTC, dracodoc wrote:
> > I have a reactive expression as data source. In my plot or DT rendering functions, I have to use the same expression again and again. Because they are inside the parameters of renderPlot, renderDataTable, I didn't find a method to assign the expression to variable first then use the variable later.

> > I'm wondering if this usage will have a performance penalty. I felt it shouldn't but my app is becoming slower when I have more features and reactive expression usage added.

> > Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: creating a reactive object that only triggers events when its value changes
messages.subject_clean: creating a reactive object that only triggers events when its value changes
messages.body_plain:
The point is fast() is dependent on input$obs:
it gets invalidated each time input$obs changes, it runs again, even if it returns the same value.
slow() also gets invalidated because it depends on fast() that got invalidated.

So you can try using reactiveValues as follows (Note: I made some changes in the code to make it shorter for now):
define values <- reactiveValues(val="") to hold the value you will use
update values$val when fast() changes

If you uncomment print("here"), you will see it slow() will get evaluated when the value changes, not every time it gets recalculated.

ui <- fluidPage(

  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      sliderInput("obs",
                  "Number of observations (low = red, high = blue)",
                  min = 10, max = 500, value = 100)

    ),

    mainPanel(plotOutput("slow"),
              verbatimTextOutput("f"))
  )
)

server <- function(input, output){

  ## fast ---------------------------------------
  fast <- reactive({
    # this is fast
    ifelse(input$obs > 200,"y","x")
  })

  ## reactive values -----------------------------
  values <- reactiveValues(val="")

  observeEvent(fast(),{
    values$val=fast()
  })

  ## slow: render plot ---------------------------
  output$slow <- renderPlot({
    # print("here")  #for debugging
    plot(1, 1, cex = 10, pch = 19, col = ifelse(values$val=="x","red","blue"))

  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

messages.body_plain:
Joe,
Would this be a good suggestion for a reusable function?

## function: duplicatedRecative values -----------------------------
duplicatedRecative <- function(signal)
{
  values <- reactiveValues(val="")

  observe({
    s <- signal()
    isolate(values$val <- s)
  })

  reactive(values$val)
}

## UI -------------------------------------------------------------------

ui <- fluidPage(

  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      sliderInput("obs",
                  "Number of observations (low = red, high = blue)",
                  min = 10, max = 500, value = 100)

    ),
    mainPanel(plotOutput("slow")

    )
  )
)

## Server ----------------------------------------------

server <- function(input, output){

  ## fast ---------------------------------------
  fast <- reactive({
    # this is fast
    ifelse(input$obs > 200,"y","x")
  })

  ## reactive value dependent on fast --------------------
  colx <- duplicatedRecative(fast)

  ## slow: render plot -------------------------------------
  output$slow <- renderPlot({

    print("here")  #for debugging

    plot(1, 1, cex = 10, pch = 19, col = ifelse(colx()=="x","red","blue"))

  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

Joe,
Thanks.
Is there a preference of either "reactiveBinding" or "reactiveValues"?

On Sunday, February 12, 2017 at 9:45:46 PM UTC+2, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> Ah, knew I had done that pretty recently!
>
> Omayma, looks good except you don't need that isolate--only reading a reactive value is a reactive operation, writing a reactive value is not.
> On Sun, Feb 12, 2017 at 11:41 AM Dean Attali <daat...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > Your solution seems to be extremely similar to what Joe himself recommended to me a few months ago:
> > https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/1484#issuecomment-262812760
> >
> > (except he used a reactiveBinding instead of reactiveValues)
> >
> >
> > On Saturday, 11 February 2017 15:28:56 UTC-5, omayma Said wrote:
> > > Joe,
> > > Would this be a good suggestion for a reusable function?
> > >
> > >
> > > ## function: duplicatedRecative values -----------------------------
> > > duplicatedRecative <- function(signal)
> > > {
> > >   values <- reactiveValues(val="")
> > >
> > >   observe({
> > >     s <- signal()
> > >     isolate(values$val <- s)
> > >   })
> > >
> > >   reactive(values$val)
> > > }
> > >
> > >
> > > ## UI -------------------------------------------------------------------
> > > ui <- fluidPage(
> > >
> > >   sidebarLayout(
> > >     sidebarPanel(
> > >       sliderInput("obs",
> > >                   "Number of observations (low = red, high = blue)",
> > >                   min = 10, max = 500, value = 100)
> > >
> > >     ),
> > >     mainPanel(plotOutput("slow")
> > >     )
> > >   )
> > > )
> > >
> > >
> > > ## Server ----------------------------------------------

> > >
> > >   ## fast ---------------------------------------
> > >   fast <- reactive({
> > >     # this is fast
> > >     ifelse(input$obs > 200,"y","x")
> > >   })
> > >
> > >
> > >   ## reactive value dependent on fast --------------------
> > >   colx <- duplicatedRecative(fast)
> > >
> > >
> > >   ## slow: render plot -------------------------------------
> > >   output$slow <- renderPlot({
> > >     print("here")  #for debugging
> > >     plot(1, 1, cex = 10, pch = 19, col = ifelse(colx()=="x","red","blue"))
> > >
> > >   })
> > > }
> > >
> > > shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
> > >
> > >
> > >
> > > On Saturday, February 11, 2017 at 9:57:26 PM UTC+2, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> > > > Omayma is exactly right! You could take it a step further and wrap this idiom in a reusable function that takes a reactive and returns a "deduplicated" reactive.

> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > > ui <- fluidPage(
> > > > >
> > > > >   sidebarLayout(
> > > > >     sidebarPanel(
> > > > >       sliderInput("obs",
> > > > >                   "Number of observations (low = red, high = blue)",
> > > > >                   min = 10, max = 500, value = 100)
> > > > >
> > > > >     ),
> > > > >
> > > > >     mainPanel(plotOutput("slow"),
> > > > >               verbatimTextOutput("f"))
> > > > >   )
> > > > > )
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > > server <- function(input, output){
> > > > >
> > > > >   ## fast ---------------------------------------
> > > > >   fast <- reactive({
> > > > >     # this is fast
> > > > >     ifelse(input$obs > 200,"y","x")
> > > > >   })
> > > > >
> > > > >   ## reactive values -----------------------------
> > > > >   values <- reactiveValues(val="")
> > > > >
> > > > >   observeEvent(fast(),{
> > > > >     values$val=fast()
> > > > >   })
> > > > >
> > > > >   ## slow: render plot ---------------------------
> > > > >   output$slow <- renderPlot({
> > > > >     # print("here")  #for debugging

> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > >   })
> > > > > }
> > > > >
> > > > > shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > >

> > > > > > My problem is that the slow function executes whenever I change the value of the observer, EVEN IF the output of the fast function does not change. For example, if I change the value of the input slider from 100 to 150, the value of fast() does not change, it is still "x". But slow() will re-execute anyway.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > In other words, I would like to create an object ("fast") that behaves like an input observer, so that it only causes the re-execution of one of its dependencies when its VALUE changes, not every time this value is re-calculated.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > I hope I've explained this clearly enough, and that there's not an obvious answer already out there, such as that I missed something basic about reactive programming in Shiny...
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Thank you,
> > > > > > Daniel
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > > server <- function(input, output){
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > >      fast <- reactive({
> > > > > >
> > > > > >       obs <- input$obs
> > > > > >
> > > > > > # this is fast

> > > > > >
> > > > > >          return("y")
> > > > > >
> > > > > >       else
> > > > > >
> > > > > >          return("x")
> > > > > >
> > > > > >    })
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > >    output$slow <- renderPlot({
> > > > > >
> > > > > >       if (fast() == "x"){
> > > > > >
> > > > > > # this is slow
> > > > > >
> > > > > >          return(plot(1, 1, cex = 10, pch = 19, col = "red"))
> > > > > >
> > > > > >       }
> > > > > >
> > > > > >       if (fast() == "y"){
> > > > > >
> > > > > > # this is slow
> > > > > >
> > > > > >          return(plot(1, 1, cex = 10, pch = 19, col = "blue"))
> > > > > >
> > > > > >       }
> > > > > >
> > > > > >    })
> > > > > >
> > > > > > }
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > > ui <- fluidPage(
> > > > > >
> > > > > >    sidebarLayout(
> > > > > >
> > > > > >       sidebarPanel(
> > > > > >
> > > > > >          sliderInput("obs", "Number of observations (low = red, high = blue)", min = 10, max = 500, value = 100)
> > > > > >
> > > > > >          ),
> > > > > >
> > > > > >       mainPanel(plotOutput("slow"))
> > > > > >
> > > > > >    )
> > > > > >
> > > > > > )
> > > > > >
> > > > > >

messages.subject_clean: Scoping Question with RColorBrewer
messages.body_plain:
I'm making an module that uses some graphing functions that need RColorBrewer to work as needed. I didn't write the graphing functions and would like to avoid re-writing them if possible.

I've been successful at producing a module that incorporates these graphing functions but it only works when I define the functions, palettes and modules in the same script as the ui and server functions. When I try to incorporate my module into a larger app I get an error message claiming that the palettes I've defined (cc2 and cc1) don't exist. I think I just need to change around where I define my functions and palettes but I'm not sure what would make sense.

Here are the relevant code blocks (note that <PARAMS> is an approximation and not to be taken literally):

# DEFINE COLOR PALETTES
# (currently encoded in the server component of my_Module)
require(RColorBrewer)
reds = brewer.pal(6, 'PuRd')
greens = brewer.pal(6, 'Blues')
yellows = brewer.pal(7, 'Greys')

cc2 = c(reds[4], yellows[3], greens[4])
cc1 = c(reds[4:2], yellows[3:2], greens[3:1])

# GRAPHING FUNCTIONS
# (currently encoded in a separate file that gets sourced inside of server.R before the shinyServer() call)
my_graphing_function = function(<PARAMS>) {
  ...
  barplot(data, beside = F, col = cc1, las = 2, border = NA)
  legend('topleft', legend = rev(rownames(data[type.order,])), fill = rev(cc1))
  ...
}

# DEFINE MODULE
# (currently encoded in a separate file that gets sourced inside of server.R within the shinyServer() call)
my_Module = function(input, output, session, <PARAMS>) {
  ...
  output$my_barplot = renderPlot({
    my_graphing_function(<PARAMS>)
  ...
  })
}

For the sake of completeness, this is what my server.R code looks like:

library(shiny)
library(RColorBrewer)
# other libraries

source("Modules.R") # contains my_Module() as well as my_ModuleUI()
source("Graphing_Functions.R") # contains graphing_function() as well as others

# IMPORT DATA
my_data = read.csv("Data.csv")

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  callModule(my_Module, "NAMESPACE", <PARAMS>)
})

Again, the module and graphing functions all worked together swimmingly when everything was defined inside the same R-script but as soon as I split the code into separate files my graphing functions can't find the color palettes that have been defined within the same module.

Appreciate any and all help.

messages.subject: Display a variable number of plots based on a conditional analysis
messages.subject_clean: Display a variable number of plots based on a conditional analysis
messages.body_plain:
Hi all, I'm trying to create a Shiny app that will allow the user to select some input parameters, perform an analysis based on the inputs, and then output the results of the analysis in the form of a variable number of plots. (I posted this question on Stack Exchange <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/42120195/shiny-display-a-variable-number-of-plots-based-on-a-conditional-analysis> last week but to no avail)

The idea is that the user sets the analysis running using an action button, and then if anything interesting is found (depending on certain conditions of the analysis and the input parameters), x number of plots are generated and then displayed on the screen. x is usually somewhere between 0 (nothing interesting found) and 20 (20 interesting results found), but ultimately x is unbounded.

I've had a look here: Shiny: Dynamic Number of Output Elements/Plots <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/31686773/shiny-dynamic-number-of-output-elements-plots>, here: Shiny example app with dynamic number of plots <https://gist.github.com/wch/5436415/>, and here: Dynamic number of reactive plots with shiny <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/24497134/dynamic-number-of-reactive-plots-with-shiny> amongst other places, but I'm very new to Shiny and so I'm really struggling to make it all work. I've had some limited success in plotting variable numbers of images/graphs, but I've had no success in plotting the images in 'real time' as my analysis is running.

The code for the analysis is an R-script which I have written in the past, and I'm trying to adapt it to Shiny. It's fairly long and uses several functions. I've managed to get the script to run within Shiny, but the only thing I can't do is print the results to screen.

Here's my (pseudo)code (with most of the analysis stuff stripped out because it isn't really relevant):

ui.R:
shinyUI(fluidPage( titlePanel(title=div(img(src="logo.png"))), sidebarLayout( sidebarPanel( h3("Select analysis parameters"), # Select date range for analysis dateRangeInput("dates", "Date range", start = "2016-10-01", end = as.character(Sys.Date())), # Specify some variable related to the analysis sliderInput("var1", label = h3("Variable 1"), min = 1, max = 20, value = 10), # Begin analysis actionButton("do","Run Scan") ), mainPanel( # I want my analysis results images to be displayed here. The results are generated using plot() and the number of plots is variable. ) ) ))

server.R

# Define server logic shinyServer(function(input, output, session) { observeEvent(input$do, { # Start analysis that looks at 10 test cases for (i in 1:10) { # Perform analysis that fills the 'pattern' dataframe with a variable number of rows... # <code snipped for brevity> # Then plot the results of the analysis if anything interesting has been found and save to disk... if(nrow(patterns) > 0){ for(i in 1:nrow(patterns)){ # Results from each test case save as a different image mypath <- file.path("C:/MyFolder/ShinyImage",paste(patterns$name[i],"_", i, ".png", sep = "")) png(file=mypath) # plot the results *THESE ARE THE IMAGES THAT I WANT TO PRINT TO SCREEN* plot(whatever_has_been_found) dev.off() } } } }) })

Ideally the result plots would pop up in real time as the analysis is running, but an alternative would be for the analysis to complete and then display all of the plots.

Any help on this problem would be very much appreciated! Thank you in advance.

messages.body_plain:
You need to use a more complex css selector (not just an id). You have to inspect the html to understand it. Here's a minimal example:

ui <- fluidPage(
    useShinyjs(),
    checkboxGroupInput("variable", "Variables to show:",
        c("Cylinders" = "cyl",
            "Transmission" = "am",
            "Gears" = "gear")),
    actionButton("btn", "Disable 'Cylinder' variable"),
    tableOutput("data")
)

server <- function(input, output) {
    output$data <- renderTable({
        head(mtcars[, c("mpg", input$variable), drop = FALSE])
    }, rownames = TRUE)

    observeEvent(input$btn, {
        shinyjs::disable(selector = "#variable input[value='cyl']")
    })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

messages.body_plain:
Hi Guys,

I've made an interactive leaflet map using R Shiny. I was wondering if it was possible to hover over a polygon on the map and it displays certain information inside that polygon.

Ideally I would like something like this: http://leafletjs.com/examples/choropleth/

Here is my code:

library(shinydashboard)
library(shiny)
library(leaflet.extras)
library(maps)
library(shinyjs)
library(rgdal)

library(leaflet.extras)
library(leaflet)
setwd("D:\\ASMA\\Work\\R scripts\\Dashboard")

global<-function(){
  regionn<-read.csv("region.csv")
  regiongeo<- readOGR(dsn = "region.geojson", layer = "OGRGeoJSON")
  regiongeo<<-regiongeo
  regionn<<-regionn
}

server <- function(input, output) {
output$map = renderLeaflet({
    leaflet() %>% addTiles(urlTemplate = "http://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png <http://tile.openstreetmap.org/%7Bz%7D/%7Bx%7D/%7By%7D.png>") %>% #,options = tileOptions()) %>%
      setView(lng = -79.3832, lat = 43.6532 , zoom = 6, options = list(maxzoom = 5)) %>%
      addPolygons(data = regiongeo, layerId = "region",fillOpacity = 0, weight = 2.5)})

  labels<- paste("Region: " ,regionn$region_cd,"\n",
                 "Maximum CVA: ",regionn$max_cva, sep ="\n")
  observeEvent(input$map_zoom,{
    proxy<- leafletProxy("map")
    if(input$map_zoom == 6)
    {proxy %>% addPolygons(data = regiongeo , fillOpacity = 0,weight = 2.5,highlightOptions = highlightOptions(
      color='#ff0000', opacity = 1, weight = 5.2, fillOpacity = 0,
      bringToFront = TRUE, sendToBack = TRUE),label=labels,labelOptions= labelOptions(direction = 'auto'))}})

}

body<-navbarPage("MPAC Analytics", id="nav",
           tabPanel("Interactive map",
                    div(class="outer",
                        tags$head(
                          includeCSS("styles.css"),
                          includeScript("gomap.js")
                        ),
                        leafletOutput("map", height = "100%",width = "100%"),
                        absolutePanel(id = "controls", class = "panel panel-default", fixed = TRUE,
                                      draggable = TRUE, top = 60, left = "auto", right = 20, bottom = "auto",
                                      width = 330, height = "auto",
                                      h2("Analysis Box")))))
ui2 <-body

shinyApp(ui = ui2, server = server,onStart=global)

    })

}

messages.body_plain:
It doesn't appear to be about deleting, but rather, anything that causes renderDataTable to invalidate. I tested this by putting an actionButton in the UI, and referring to it from within the renderDataTable. Once the button is clicked, the numeric inputs don't work.

I think the problem is that Shiny.unbindAll isn't called right before the table is replaced, so all the old bindings are still active, and the new numericInputs therefore can't be bound because they share the same input IDs. I'm cc-ing Yihui who might have a better idea about how to handle this.

I will also say that this appears to be a bit of an awkward fit for DT anyway, you might consider rhandsontable instead (I actually don't know that much about rhandsontable but it looks like it's intended for what you're doing in this example).

messages.subject_clean: showing a shiny app in html (shinyAppDir, iframe) does not work anymore after switching to https??
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I installed SSL certificates on both my shiny server and my webserver.
My application runs fine at https://bsohtools.tk/shiny/co2sim/ when accessing it directly.

Before installing the SSL certificates, I could run the application in a iframe on the website of our society: https://www.bsoh.be/?q=nl/shiny/ and in ioslides presentations from rmarkdown files.

However, after installing the certificates, it does not show up anymore on my website nor in my slides.

When running the app directly from rstudio server in a chrome browser using the play button with the code

```{r}
shinyAppDir("/srv/shiny-server/co2sim/")
```

and then "open in browser", the app runs like expected.

When knitting an rmarkdown to a shiny interactive document and then "open in browser" (chrome), the presentation runs, but it shows the code for shinyAppDir and a blank rectangle for the iframe. Does anybody know what is going on and why the shiny gallery https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/217592607-Can-I-embed-shiny-apps-in-other-websites-e-g-iFrames- eg https://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/superzip-example.html
is full of similar examples and why I can't get this to work?

Many thanks,
Tom

messages.subject_clean: showing a shiny app in html (shinyAppDir, iframe) does not work anymore after switching to https??
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,
Found the solution...

In the webserver configuration, you should set the X-Frame options to ALLOWALL in the location headers.
For me, this had to be done for the nginx, locations /shiny/ and /rstudio/.

After adding

add_header X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL;

as the last line in both sections, the application loaded fine in iframes and html5 presentations.
Kind regards,
Tom.

messages.subject: ShinyBS: using conditionals to toggle bsModals
messages.subject_clean: ShinyBS: using conditionals to toggle bsModals
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm in the process of building a shinyapp that is one part data entry and the other part is for data vis. Before visuals, the data must be pass validation. To best describe the issue, I've provided an simplified demo app and a description of what the app is doing.

Purpose

In the demo app ("Shiny App-les" - I couldn't resist) below, the user is asked to enter their name, the date the apples purchased, the number of apples bought, and the number of apples were eaten. During the validation phase, I'm running the following checks (on observeEvent()).

1. Was a name provided?
2. Was the date the apples were purchased greater than today's date?
3. Apples must be greater than 1.
4. Apples eaten cannot be greater than the number purchased.

Methods

I'm using the functions bsModal() and toggleModal() from the shinyBS package to present the messages for each error. I'm using shinyBS over shinyJS in this instance as I intended to display other information (tables, plots, etc.) in each modal. I know the createAlert() will accomplish the same thing (and works), but again I anticipating doing much more with the modals.

The Issue

Here's where I'm experiencing an issue.

Try clicking the 'submit' button without entering any information. You will notice that the final bsModal ("Yum. Hope you enjoyed the apples!") will appear first even though you haven't entered any information. If you click "close", you will see the error message ("Please provide a name.").  If you enter a name and then enter a date greater than today, the final bsModal message will appear.  This occurs for every scenario where an error could occur.

Troubleshooting

I've attempted the following:

- Commenting the last modal, will not solve the issue. It will simply cause the modal before to trigger instead.

- When shinyjs::alert()s are enabled in each condition (and commenting modals), the messages appear as you might expect. I've left the shinyjs lines in (but commented) for those who are interested.

- I tried to control the behavior of the "else" statement by creating a object that counted the items correct (or valid). The final condition would trigger only if that items correct was equal to the total possible points (in this case 4). I was finding this approach too time consuming and was unable to get it fully working.

Summary

Any thoughts on what could be the culprit?

- David

library(shiny)
library(shinyBS)
library(lubridate)
#library(shinyjs)

# make ui
ui <- fluidPage(

    # shinyjs - to test the server side logic, comment shinyBS chunks
    # shinyjs::useShinyjs(),

    # general text
    titlePanel("Shiny App-les"),
    helpText("Enter information in the form below."),

    #/////////////////////////
    # item 1: enter your name
    fluidRow(
        # item
        column(1, p("1.")),
        # question
        column(2, p("Enter your name")),
        #
        column(2, textInput("name", label= NULL))
    ),

    # error message for item 1
    bsModal(

        # modal params
        id = "error_item1", title = "Oops!",
        trigger = "formButton", size = "small",

        # content
        p("Please provide a name.")
    ),

    #/////////////////////////
    # item 2: what's today's date?
    fluidRow(
        # item
        column(1, p("2.")),
        # question
        column(2, p("Enter your name")),
        #
        column(2, dateInput("today", label = NULL,value = Sys.Date()))
    ),

    # error message for item 2
    bsModal(
        # modal params
        id = "error_item2", title = "Oops!",
        trigger = "formButton", size = "small",

        # content
        p("Date supplied cannot be greater than today.")
    ),

    #/////////////////////////
    # item 3: # of apples purchased
    fluidRow(
        # item
        column(1, p("3.")),
        # question
        column(2, p("How many apples did you buy?")),
        #
        column(2, numericInput("num1", label = NULL,
                               value = 0, min  = 0,
                               max = 10, step = 1))

    ),

    # error message for item 3
    bsModal(
        # modal params
        id = "error_item3", title = "Oops!",
        trigger = "formButton", size = "small",

        # content
        p("You forgot apples!")
    ),

    #/////////////////////////
    # item 4: # of apples eaten
    fluidRow(
        # item
        column(1, p("4.")),
        # question
        column(2, p("How many apples did you eat?")),
        #
        column(2, numericInput("num2", label = NULL,
                               value = 0, min = 0,
                               max = 10, step = 1))
    ),

    # error message for item 4
    bsModal(
        # modal params
        id = "error_item4", title = "Oops!",
        trigger = "formButton", size = "small",

        # content
        p("You cannot eat more apples than you purchased!")
    ),

    #/////////////////////////
    # button
    actionButton(inputId = "formButton", label = "Enter"),

    # status complete!
    bsModal(
        # modal params
        id = "apples_complete", title = "Yum!",
        trigger = "formButton", size = "small",

        # content
        p("Hope you enjoyed the apples!")
    )
)

# server
server <- function(input, output, session){

    # validate entry only when button clicked
    observeEvent(input$formButton,{

        # get inputs
        name <- as.character(input$name)
        tdate <- format(as.Date(input$today), "%Y-%m-%d")
        num1 <- as.numeric(input$num1)
        num2 <- as.numeric(input$num2)

        # catch errors: item 1 - no name supplied
        if(name == ""){
            toggleModal(session, modalId = "error_item1", toggle = "open")
            #shinyjs::alert("Name not given.")
        }

        # catch errors: item 2 - date is greater than today
        else if(tdate > today()){
            toggleModal(session, modalId = "error_item2", toggle = "open")
            #shinyjs::alert("Date cannot be greater than today.")
        }

        # catch errors: item 3 - no apples purchased
        else if(num1 == 0){
            toggleModal(session, modalId = "error_item3", toggle = "open")
            #shinyjs::alert("You forgot to get apples!")
        }

        # catch errors: item 4 - eaten > purchased
        else if(num2 > input$num1){
            toggleModal(session, modalId = "error_item4", toggle = "open")
            #shinyjs::alert("You ate more apples than your purchased?")
        }

        # no errors
        else {
            toggleModal(session, modalId = "apples_complete", toggle = "open")
            #shinyjs::alert("Apples are delicious!")
        }
    })

}

# launch
shinyApp(ui, server)

messages.body_plain:
Hi.

I'm new with Shiny but not that new with R.
I'm building an app for work that will eventually help with forecasting.
For this, I will need several packages like ggplot2, forecast, etc.

However, I'm having trouble when deploying my app to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> (even though it works locally).
I also wanted to use lubridate but it gave me the same error so I used another function. I don't know what I'm missing please help.

Here is my code (sorry for the bad syntax and unnecessary code, I will clean it later)

#Comienzo la aplicación

#Cargo las librerías
require(shiny)
require(rsconnect)
require(ggplot2)

#Cambio el directorio (solo lo uso si lo voy a correr local)
#setwd("C:/Users/borja.sanz/Desktop/Borja/R/Shiny/Directorio - Proyecciones Productos")

#Cargo los datos
data<-read.csv("./data/Pruebas.Shiny.csv")

#Cambio las fechas a formato de fecha
data$Fecha = as.POSIXct(data$Fecha, format = "%d/%m/%Y")

#Extraigo el año
data$Año = as.factor(format(data$Fecha, "%Y"))

#Quito comas de los numeros (si hay)
data$Unidades = as.numeric(gsub(",","",data$Unidades))

#-------------------------------------------------------------------
#Comienzo la interfaz de usuario
ui <-

    shinyUI(tabsetPanel(
    tabPanel("Producto Comparativo",pageWithSidebar(
    headerPanel("Proyecciones de Productos"),
    #Creo los inputs del sidebar
      sidebarPanel(uiOutput("pais"),
                   uiOutput("año"),
                   uiOutput("producto.maestro"),
                   uiOutput("producto"),
                   uiOutput("fecha.promo"),
                   uiOutput("duracion")),

      mainPanel(textOutput("total.unidades"),
                plotOutput("grafica.comparativo"))

  )
),
    tabPanel("Producto a proyectar")
)
)

#Comienzo el archivo de servidor

server <- function(input, output) {
require(ggplot2)
require(shiny)

  output$pais = renderUI(selectInput(inputId = "pais",
                                     label = "Producto a comparar",
                                     choices = c("Seleccione un país",levels(data$Pais)),
                                     selected = "Seleccione un país")
  )

  output$año = renderUI(selectInput(inputId = "año",
                                     label = NULL,
                                     choices = c("Seleccione un año",levels(data$Año)),
                                     selected = "Seleccione un año")
  )

  # output$fecha.comparativo = renderUI(
  #   dateRangeInput(inputId = "fecha.comparativo",
  #                  label = "¿Cuándo estuvo activo este producto?",
  #                  start = as.POSIXct(Sys.Date()-365),
  #                  end = as.POSIXct(Sys.Date()-1),
  #                  min = as.POSIXct("2014-01-01"),
  #                  max = as.POSIXct(Sys.Date() -1),
  #                  format = "dd/mm/yyyy",
  #                  separator = "a",
  #                  language = "es")
  # )

  output$producto.maestro = renderUI(
        selectInput(inputId = "producto.maestro",
                        label = NULL,
                        choices = c("Seleccione un producto maestro",levels(factor(data$Producto.Maestro[which(data$Pais == input$pais & data$Año == input$año)]))),
                        selected = "Seleccione un producto maestro")
  )

  output$producto = renderUI(
    if(input$pais == "Seleccione un país" || input$año == "Seleccione un año" || input$producto.maestro == "Seleccione un producto maestro"){return(NULL)
     }else selectInput(inputId = "producto",
                     label = NULL,
                     choices = levels(factor(data$Producto[which(data$Pais == input$pais & data$Año == input$año & data$Producto.Maestro == input$producto.maestro)])),
                     selected = levels(factor(data$Producto[which(data$Pais == input$pais & data$Año == input$año & data$Producto.Maestro == input$producto.maestro)])),
                     multiple = TRUE)
  )
  # output$fecha.promo = renderUI(
  #   dateRangeInput(inputId = "fecha.promo",
  #                  label = "¿Cuándo va a lanzar su promoción?",
  #                  start = as.POSIXct(Sys.Date()),
  #                  end = as.POSIXct(Sys.Date() + 45),
  #                  min = as.POSIXct(Sys.Date()),
  #                  max = as.POSIXct(Sys.Date() + 365),
  #                  format = "dd/mm/yyyy",
  #                  separator = "a",
  #                  language = "es")
  # )
  # output$duracion = renderText(paste("Duración de la promoción: ",input$fecha.promo[2] - input$fecha.promo[1]," días"))

  output$total.unidades = renderText(
    if(input$pais == "Seleccione un país" || input$año == "Seleccione un año" || input$producto.maestro == "Seleccione un producto maestro"){return()
    }else paste("Unidades vendidas del producto comparativo: ", prettyNum(sum(data$Unidades[which(data$Pais == input$pais & data$Año == input$año & data$Producto.Maestro == input$producto.maestro & data$Producto %in% input$producto)]),big.mark = ",")))

  df3 = reactive({(subset(data, data$Año == input$año & data$Pais == input$pais & data$Producto.Maestro == input$producto.maestro & data$Producto %in% input$producto))})

  df4 = reactive({(setNames(aggregate(df3()$Unidades, by=list(df3()$Producto.Maestro, df3()$Fecha),FUN =sum), c("Producto.Maestro","Fecha","Unidades")))})

output$grafica.comparativo = renderPlot(
  if(input$pais == "Seleccione un país" || input$producto.maestro == "Seleccione un producto maestro" || is.na <http://is.na>(input$producto.maestro)){return()
    } else print(ggplot(df4(), aes(x = Fecha, y = Unidades)) + geom_line(color = "black",size = 1))
  )
}

#Corro la aplicación
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

install_github("environmentalinformatics-marburg/mapview", ref = "develop")

library(shiny)
library(leaflet)
library(mapview)
# Define UI for application that draws a histogram

      # Show a plot of the generated distribution
      mainPanel(
         leafletOutput("map")
      )

)

   output$map <- renderLeaflet({
     map2 <- leaflet() %>%

       addTiles('http://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/World_Imagery/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x} <http://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/World_Imagery/MapServer/tile/%7Bz%7D/%7By%7D/%7Bx%7D>',

})

messages.subject_clean: ui.R loads but server disconnects when server.R tries to run
messages.body_plain:
I'm trying to get my first ever Shiny app up and running on Shiny Server (Open Source).

I have Shiny Server installed on an Amazon EC2 Unbuntu/Linux instance.  I built my app locally and can run it from my desktop but want to have run off the server.

When I execute my app the "ui.R" part works just fine as the graphics, slider, UI layout, etc. all pops up on the screen.  But then it "grays out" and the actual tables/plots that are defined in server.R don't show up.

In the bottom corner of my browser a box pops up that says "disconnected from server."

My biggest challenge is not being able to see a log file or know what kind of error I'm trying to debug...

Thanks for any help anyone on the list might have.

Jared

messages.subject: Re: I had created my own function in R Studio, shiny app not working on deploying
messages.subject_clean: I had created my own function in R Studio, shiny app not working on deploying
messages.body_plain:
You need to define the function in app.R (or globals.R if you're using the two-file layout), otherwise the server doesn't know which function you're talking about. A good way to test this is to restart your R session and then run the app. Then, you'll probably get the same error locally, since the function definition was somewhere in your local environment, but not in app.R (or other sourced files).

> It's showing Error: could not find the function while deploying the shiny app on server, whereas it's working fine on the local panel.
> Function is defined by me.

if (!require('leaflet')) devtools::install_github('rstudio/leaflet')
if (!require('mapview')) devtools::install_github("environmentalinformatics-marburg/mapview", ref = "develop")

messages.subject: Re: textOutput/ActionButton are not updating after executing renderText/updateActionButton
messages.subject_clean: textOutput/ActionButton are not updating after executing renderText/updateActionButton
messages.body_plain:
You can do something like this:

library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      numericInput("steps", "Time steps:", 10, min=1),

      actionButton("run", label="Start")
    ),
    mainPanel(

      textOutput("status")
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  vals <- reactiveValues(running = FALSE, step = 0, run = 1, label = "Start")

  # helper functions
  toggleLabel <- function() {
    if (vals$label %in% c("Start", "Resume")) vals$label <- "Stop"
    else vals$label <- "Resume"
    vals$label
  }

  observe({
    req(input$run)

    isolate({
      # update label when the button is clicked and stop/resume computation
      if (input$run != vals$run) {
        updateActionButton(session, "run", label = toggleLabel())
        vals$run <- input$run
        vals$running <- !vals$running
      }

      # update label and vals$running the first time around only
      if (vals$label == "Start") {
        updateActionButton(session, "run", label = toggleLabel())
        vals$running <- TRUE
      }
    })

    # If we're not done yet, then schedule this block to execute again ASAP.
    # Note that we can be interrupted by other reactive updates to, for
    # instance, update a text output.
    if (isolate({ (vals$step < input$steps) && vals$running })) {
      Sys.sleep(1) # placeholder for computation
      vals$step <- isolate(vals$step) + 1
      invalidateLater(0, session)
    }
  })

  output$status <- renderText({
    paste("You're on iteration number:", vals$step)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

This is based on Jeff Allen's gist: https://gist.github.com/trestletech/8608815

messages.body_plain:
You need to change `trigger = "formButton"` to `trigger = ""`, otherwise all modals are bound to the same element... I've copy-pasted the full working code below. Also, Shiny now supports modals natively (article here: https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/modal-dialogs.html and documentation with several examples here: https://shiny.rstudio.com/reference/shiny/latest/modalDialog.html). Not sure if this is better or worse for your case, but just FYI.

Working code:

library(shiny)
library(shinyBS)
library(lubridate)
#library(shinyjs)

# make ui
ui <- fluidPage(

  # shinyjs - to test the server side logic, comment shinyBS chunks
  # shinyjs::useShinyjs(),

  # general text
  titlePanel("Shiny App-les"),
  helpText("Enter information in the form below."),

  #/////////////////////////
  # item 1: enter your name
  fluidRow(
    # item
    column(1, p("1.")),
    # question
    column(2, p("Enter your name")),
    #
    column(2, textInput("name", label= NULL))
  ),

  # error message for item 1
  bsModal(

    # modal params
    id = "error_item1", title = "Oops!",

    trigger = "", size = "small",

    # content
    p("Please provide a name.")
  ),

  #/////////////////////////
  # item 2: what's today's date?
  fluidRow(
    # item
    column(1, p("2.")),
    # question
    column(2, p("Enter your name")),
    #
    column(2, dateInput("today", label = NULL,value = Sys.Date()))
  ),

  # error message for item 2
  bsModal(
    # modal params
    id = "error_item2", title = "Oops!",

    trigger = "", size = "small",

    # content
    p("Date supplied cannot be greater than today.")
  ),

  #/////////////////////////
  # item 3: # of apples purchased
  fluidRow(
    # item
    column(1, p("3.")),
    # question
    column(2, p("How many apples did you buy?")),
    #
    column(2, numericInput("num1", label = NULL,
      value = 0, min  = 0,
      max = 10, step = 1))

  ),

  # error message for item 3
  bsModal(
    # modal params
    id = "error_item3", title = "Oops!",

    trigger = "", size = "small",

    # content
    p("You forgot apples!")
  ),

  #/////////////////////////
  # item 4: # of apples eaten
  fluidRow(
    # item
    column(1, p("4.")),
    # question
    column(2, p("How many apples did you eat?")),
    #
    column(2, numericInput("num2", label = NULL,
      value = 0, min = 0,
      max = 10, step = 1))
  ),

  # error message for item 4
  bsModal(
    # modal params
    id = "error_item4", title = "Oops!",

    trigger = "", size = "small",

    # content
    p("You cannot eat more apples than you purchased!")
  ),

  #/////////////////////////
  # button
  actionButton(inputId = "formButton", label = "Enter"),

  # status complete!
  bsModal(
    # modal params
    id = "apples_complete", title = "Yum!",

    trigger = "", size = "small",

    # content
    p("Hope you enjoyed the apples!")
  )
)

# server
server <- function(input, output, session){

  # validate entry only when button clicked
  observeEvent(input$formButton,{

    # get inputs
    name <- as.character(input$name)
    tdate <- format(as.Date(input$today), "%Y-%m-%d")
    num1 <- as.numeric(input$num1)
    num2 <- as.numeric(input$num2)

    isolate({

      # catch errors: item 1 - no name supplied
      if(name == ""){
        toggleModal(session, modalId = "error_item1", toggle = "open")
        #shinyjs::alert("Name not given.")
      }

      # catch errors: item 2 - date is greater than today
      else if(tdate > today()){
        toggleModal(session, modalId = "error_item2", toggle = "open")
        #shinyjs::alert("Date cannot be greater than today.")
      }

      # catch errors: item 3 - no apples purchased
      else if(num1 == 0){
        toggleModal(session, modalId = "error_item3", toggle = "open")
        #shinyjs::alert("You forgot to get apples!")
      }

      # catch errors: item 4 - eaten > purchased
      else if(num2 > input$num1){
        toggleModal(session, modalId = "error_item4", toggle = "open")
        #shinyjs::alert("You ate more apples than your purchased?")
      }

      # no errors
      else {
        toggleModal(session, modalId = "apples_complete", toggle = "open")
        #shinyjs::alert("Apples are delicious!")
      }
    })
  })

}

# launch
shinyApp(ui, server)
